questions.text: Which Roman emperor is said to have fiddled while Rome burned?
questions.explanation: Tradition blames Nero, though the fiddle story is legend.

questions.text: In which country were the Great Pyramids of Giza built?
questions.explanation: The Giza pyramids stand near Cairo, Egypt.

questions.text: Who was the first Roman emperor?
questions.explanation: Octavian took the title Augustus in 27 BC.

questions.text: Which Duke of Normandy won the Battle of Hastings in 1066?
questions.explanation: William the Conqueror defeated Harold at Hastings.

questions.text: Which ancient Greek city-state was famed for its warrior society?
questions.explanation: Spartan life was organised around military training.

questions.text: Which Carthaginian general crossed the Alps with war elephants?
questions.explanation: Hannibal marched on Italy across the Alps in 218 BC.

questions.text: Which charter did King John seal at Runnymede in 1215?
questions.explanation: Magna Carta limited the king's powers.

questions.text: Which empire did Genghis Khan found?
questions.explanation: Genghis Khan united the Mongol tribes around 1206.

questions.text: Which Greek writer is often called the Father of History?
questions.explanation: Herodotus wrote the Histories about the Greco-Persian Wars.

questions.text: The Rosetta Stone helped scholars decipher which ancient script?
questions.explanation: Its parallel texts allowed Champollion to decode hieroglyphs.

questions.text: Leonidas and his Spartans famously held which pass in 480 BC?
questions.explanation: Thermopylae was the site of the stand against Xerxes' Persians.

questions.text: Which Byzantine emperor had the Hagia Sophia rebuilt in the 6th century?
questions.explanation: Justinian's Hagia Sophia was completed in 537.

questions.text: In which year did Constantinople fall to the Ottoman Turks?
questions.explanation: Mehmed II captured the city in 1453.

questions.text: Which 1071 battle saw the Seljuk Turks defeat a Byzantine army?
questions.explanation: Manzikert opened Anatolia to Turkish settlement.

questions.text: Which 843 treaty divided Charlemagne's empire among his grandsons?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Verdun split the Carolingian realm in three.

spares.text: According to Homeric legend, which city was defeated by a giant wooden horse trick?
spares.explanation: The Greeks hid soldiers inside the horse to enter Troy.

spares.text: Which Roman leader was assassinated in 44 BC on the Ides of March?
spares.explanation: Conspirators stabbed Caesar in the Senate.

spares.text: Which English king was killed at the Battle of Bosworth Field in 1485?
spares.explanation: Richard III's death ended the Wars of the Roses.
